I am 61 years old, and I have been farming this land in Quzhou County my whole life. I only went to primary school, but I know this soil and this climate better than any book. Here on the North China Plain, we follow the wheat-maize double-cropping system — that is what my father did, and that is what I will do this year. I have 5 mu of land. Right now, the winter wheat I sowed last October is in the field. It is early spring, so my immediate task is to top-dress nitrogen and irrigate as the wheat greens up. I buy improved wheat seed from the dealer in town — it is reliable and gives good yield. As soon as I harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize using the no-tillage seeder directly into the wheat stubble. There is never enough time between harvest and sowing, so we must move fast. For wheat, I apply about 22 kg of nitrogen per mu, split between base fertilizer and spring top-dressing, plus about 7 kg of phosphorus and 6 kg of potassium per mu. I irrigate the wheat three times — green-up, jointing, and heading — and spray pesticides three times for aphids and rust. For maize, I put down around 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu, irrigate twice if the summer rains are light, and spray pesticides twice for maize borers and weeds. I expect about 550 kg of wheat per mu and 650 kg of maize per mu. I do what my neighbors do; it has fed my family for decades, and I trust it.
